question: What are the two ways in which Python (and most computer languages in general) differ from languages used for communication (like English)?

answers.answer: The rules of Python are relatively straightforward and intuitive.
answers.feedback: Yes! You won't have to learn about any exceptions to any rules, and the structures of Python can be grouped into just four main categories (that you'll learn later).

answers.answer: Python has a kernel, so it has much higher capabilities than English.
answers.feedback: No! The kernel isn't part of the Python language itself, but is best thought of as the person you are speaking Python (aka giving instructions) to. And much like how you are the mind behind the words you speak, you must know what your code means and intends to do.
Yes! All Python code, no matter the location, will follow the same rules. However, if you are off by even a single character, the kernel interprets it as straight gibberish.

answers.answer: Python is very lenient about what characters you use where.
answers.feedback: No! In most cases, Python is exceptionally punishing when it comes to improperly-placed syntax (except space-bars), and this refusal to deviate from the rules is something you'll inevitably have to get used to.
